question: True or false: someone who has eaten their fill of one food will still eat more when a different food appears?
answer: True. Barbara Rolls showed that the pleasure of a food falls as it is eaten while other foods stay appealing, an effect called sensory-specific satiety. Volunteers full of one dish ate more when a different one was offered. It is why dessert finds room after a big main course, and why buffets defeat good intentions.
move: Variety resets appetite, so limit the choices rather than test the willpower.
ask: When I keep eating, is it hunger, or just something new on the table?
trap: Fullness means a full stomach, whatever food comes next.
reference: Rolls BJ, Rolls ET, Rowe EA, Sweeney K, Sensory specific satiety in man, Physiology & Behavior, 1981
